existing_capabilities.fact: The dashboard already has validated create-once corpus campaign registration, append-only writer-owned events, immutable result projection, a loopback service, and scoped browser capabilities.
Local single-case and suite execution have supported launch boundaries and create run directories before candidate execution.
Distributed evaluation already has validated package, matrix, dispatch, stage, result, accounting, and exact execution identity records.
Completed local suites already contain selected cases, planned and actual attempts, per-case outcomes, overall outcome, timing, accounting, treatment identity, and skill identity.
The cumulative hill-climb requires minimization of each newly added task increment before publication and preserves earlier wins.
Generalization requires separately labeled development, regression, and genuinely unexposed transfer cases. Source tasks cannot become held out again after influencing changes.

observed_failures.failure: Every registered agent session can open another browser tab.
observed_failures.cause: dashboard_cli.py::register_dashboard uses session opened_at rather than project and service-generation state.

observed_failures.failure: Refreshing a page can show Missing browser capability.
observed_failures.cause: The static client removes the fragment capability and does not retain it in tab-scoped browser state.

observed_failures.failure: Retry corpora appear as separate top-level campaigns.
observed_failures.cause: The projection and routes have corpus campaign identity but no explicit project identity.

observed_failures.failure: An active or completed suite can appear as if no evaluator run occurred.
observed_failures.cause: The live view uses agent-session heartbeat events and waits for final suite artifacts instead of following evaluator-owned suite lifecycle.

observed_failures.failure: The campaign page exposes many empty or unavailable schema fields instead of the user's improvement goal.
observed_failures.cause: The prior product hierarchy treats storage records as primary user objects.

hard_boundaries.constraint: The dashboard remains read-only and cannot launch, cancel, mutate, approve, or publish evaluations.
Hidden judge references, criteria, prompts, private packets, and answer-shaped evidence remain unavailable through every projection and route.
True holdout identities and behavioral failure details cannot influence the optimizing agent.
Project, task, case, and run grouping is explicit. Names, paths, timestamps, and suffixes are not identity evidence.
Immutable evaluator results outrank live or session records. Liveness never implies PASS, FAIL, or completion.
Unknown and partial accounting remains labeled. The dashboard cannot present incomplete totals as exact.
Legacy corpora without explicit project metadata are not auto-grouped or auto-migrated.
Unsupported custom launch paths may be absent. Supported evaluator launchers are the automatic monitoring boundary.

included: automatic local and distributed run lifecycle
time, run, attempt, token, and cost rollups
